rationale: B wins by a nose because it finds the public-company story the update hands you and keeps it separate from retail ops: "Allbirds posts its first gross-margin improvement as the turnaround plan starts to bite" has a real markets desk behind it. A is cleaner, but its refusal of "Can one good quarter win back investors holding Allbirds below its IPO price?" throws away a valid protagonist and calls it a duplicate. B still smuggles in some outside DTC context, so this is a slight win, not a parade.
gaps_in_A: "Can one good quarter win back investors holding Allbirds below its IPO price?" — calling this a duplicate is too severe. Public, unprofitable, below-IPO-price Allbirds creates a distinct markets/investor angle, not just a footnote in the retail-ops story.

"Allbirds posts its first gross-margin gain after closing stores and cutting 40% of its products" folds merchandising, store closures, margin, and public-company context into one bucket. Useful, but it leaves a sharper assortment-strategy angle on the table.
"making a wholesale partnership a centerpiece of its relaunch" overstates the supplied fact. The update says the named wholesale partnership is part of the relaunch; "centerpiece" needs proof.
"Story type: category-creation" is too grand for one company’s unverified durability claim. The body handles the caveat well, but the label is inflated.
gaps_in_B: "The prevailing belief in DTC retail is that growth comes from expanding the range and the store footprint" is outside the supplied facts. Make it a reporter question or prove it; don’t present it as given.
"a brand that built itself on direct retail" and "DTC-to-wholesale shift" smuggle in Allbirds history not present in the update. Plausible is not the same as grounded.
"durability is the chronic knock against natural-material shoes" may be true, but it is not in the update. Either source it or keep the hook to Allbirds’ own original-runner comparison.
"Story type: funding-mechanics" is the wrong label. This is an equity/markets turnaround angle, not a funding story. Sloppy labels make good angles look machine-stamped.
